courses.title: Python Programming
courses.description: Learn Python from the beginning through practical coding exercises and a final project.
outcomes: Understand the core concepts of python programming
Apply your skills through practical exercises
Evaluate your work and improve with feedback
Complete a project you can share in your portfolio

lessons.title: Introduction to Python
lessons.content: Python is a readable, general-purpose programming language. A program is a sequence of instructions. Start with print('Hello, Learnova!') and observe the output. Indentation groups statements into blocks; keep indentation consistent.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates introduction to python. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Installing Python
lessons.content: Install Python from its official distribution and verify the interpreter with python --version. Create a project folder and a virtual environment with python -m venv .venv. A virtual environment keeps project dependencies separate.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates installing python. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.content: Variables give names to values: name = 'Aisha', age = 20, and enrolled = True. Common types include strings, integers, floats, and booleans. Use type(value) to inspect a type and explicit conversions such as int('20') when appropriate.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates variables and data types. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Operators
lessons.content: Arithmetic operators include +, -, *, /, //, and %. Comparisons such as == and > return booleans. Combine conditions with and, or, and not. Use parentheses to make the order of evaluation clear.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates operators. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Conditional Statements
lessons.content: Use if, elif, and else to choose a branch. Each condition ends with a colon, followed by an indented block. For example, if score >= 70: can select a passing message. Test values at the boundary as well as values on either side.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates conditional statements. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.content: A for loop visits items in a sequence, while a while loop repeats as long as its condition is true. range(5) produces numbers from 0 to 4. Update the condition of a while loop to avoid an infinite loop.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates loops. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.content: Define reusable behavior with def. Parameters receive input and return sends a result to the caller. A function should have a clear purpose. For example, def total(a, b): followed by return a + b adds two numbers.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates functions. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Lists and Dictionaries
lessons.content: Lists are ordered collections, such as scores = [75, 90, 82]. Indexes begin at zero. Dictionaries associate keys with values, such as student = {'name': 'Aisha', 'score': 90}. Choose a list for a sequence and a dictionary for named lookup.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates lists and dictionaries. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Object-Oriented Programming
lessons.content: A class groups related data and behavior. __init__ initializes an instance and self refers to that instance. Model a Student with a name and scores, then add a method that calculates the average. Keep methods focused and avoid unnecessary inheritance.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates object-oriented programming. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

lessons.title: Final Project
lessons.content: Bring the course concepts together in a command-line learning tracker. Accept input, validate it, store course information in a dictionary, and calculate completion. Split behavior into functions and test invalid input as well as the normal path.
lessons.exercise: Create a small example that demonstrates final project. Explain your approach in three to five sentences, test the result, and record one improvement you would make.

quiz.question: Which function displays output in Python?
quiz.explanation: print() sends text and values to the output.

quiz.question: Which command checks the installed Python version?
quiz.explanation: The --version option displays the interpreter version.

quiz.question: Which value is a string?
quiz.explanation: Text enclosed in quotes is a string.

quiz.question: Which operator checks equality?
quiz.explanation: == compares values; = assigns a value.

quiz.question: Which keyword starts a conditional branch?
quiz.explanation: if evaluates a condition to select a branch.

quiz.question: What values does range(3) produce?
quiz.explanation: range starts at zero and excludes the stop value.

quiz.question: Which keyword defines a function?
quiz.explanation: def declares a named Python function.

quiz.question: Which list index refers to the first item?
quiz.explanation: Python lists use zero-based indexing.

quiz.question: Which structure associates keys with values?
quiz.explanation: A dictionary maps keys to corresponding values.

quiz.question: What does self refer to in an instance method?
quiz.explanation: self is the instance on which the method is called.

assignment.title: Python Programming: Practical Project
assignment.instructions: Create a practical project applying the concepts from Python Programming. Describe the problem, explain your approach, and include evidence of your result. Submit a 200–500 word reflection and optionally attach your project. Assessment: understanding (40%), practical application (40%), and clarity (20%).

quiz.question: What makes a study goal useful?
quiz.explanation: Concrete outcomes make progress visible.

quiz.question: What is active recall?
quiz.explanation: Recall practice helps strengthen learning.

quiz.question: What is spaced practice?
quiz.explanation: Spacing gives repeated opportunities to retrieve knowledge.

quiz.question: What supports sustained focus?
quiz.explanation: Planned intervals help manage attention.

quiz.question: Why reflect after a study session?
quiz.explanation: Reflection helps adjust the next session.

quiz.question: How should a large task be planned?
quiz.explanation: Smaller steps make the work manageable.

quiz.question: What should a weekly plan include?
quiz.explanation: Realistic planning supports consistency.

quiz.question: What is useful feedback?
quiz.explanation: Specific guidance makes feedback actionable.

quiz.question: What helps track progress?
quiz.explanation: Recording outcomes makes growth visible.

quiz.question: What makes a learning habit sustainable?
quiz.explanation: Manageable practice is easier to sustain.
